title: Sustainable European Mountain Entrepreneurship Through Statistical, Neural Network, and Fractal Analyzes—A Review
content: The article explores the key dimensions of European mountain entrepreneurship, emphasizing the economic roles of the Industry (secondary sector) and Services (tertiary sector). The analysis aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of entrepreneurial support sectors in mountain regions, including commerce, automotive, transport, storage, finance, and real estate. These sectors collectively represent a substantial share of mountain-based economic activity, comprising over one-third of all enterprises in these areas, with a steady rise in their numbers. Across EU countries, the level of entropy in mountain entrepreneurship within these supporting sectors underscores the need for better structural coherence at the community level. Fractal simulations offer innovative perspectives on the organizational dynamics of mountain entrepreneurship in Europe. Furthermore, neural network models reveal patterns highlighting weak links within these supporting sectors compared to the broader secondary and tertiary sectors, while also identifying robust interconnections between these two sectors. The authors propose actionable strategies to strengthen interconnectivity among European countries based on these findings.
